The statement is modestly hawkish and growth-negative. By lifting the federal funds target to 4.75–5.00% and maintaining balance-sheet runoff caps ($60B Treasuries, $35B MBS), the FOMC is operating in clearly restrictive territory. The Committee also flags tighter credit conditions from recent banking stress. Insights from the Federal Reserve’s Financial Stability Report (FSR) reinforce the downside risks: the Survey of Salient Risks highlights persistent inflation and monetary tightening as top concerns; higher rates weigh on credit quality (notably in leveraged loans and CRE), and SLOOS-based evidence points to tighter lending standards. The FSR also notes vulnerabilities from market liquidity strains in Treasuries and from NBFIs, which could amplify shocks even if the banking system remains “sound and resilient.” Operational details—IOER at 4.9% and ON RRP at 4.8%—support transmission via administered rates, but the combination of restrictive policy and tightening credit suggests a greater drag on activity and hiring, with disinflation likely to follow. Net: elevated downside risks to growth and risk assets, offset by a credible anti-inflation stance.
